answer: A sybil defense is to tie each agent's earning power to verifiable history instead of how many identities it can spawn. A new agent must build an atlas of completed work, deliveries and attestations, before it earns full rewards, so a fresh clone starts with nothing. Reputation should accumulate like nectar gathered slowly over many honest rounds, not bought in bulk, and decay when the agent goes idle or misbehaves. One honest agent then climbs a spiral of trust, while an attacker running a hundred empty shells must repeat the same costly work for each one, making a sybil flood unprofitable.
